regulation.name: Regulation Set M-C
regulation.start_note: Live 8 Sep 2026 7:00 PM PDT — 1 Dec 2026 5:59 PM PST

formats.name: Doubles
formats.note: The official VGC format. Register 6, select 4 at team preview.

formats.name: Singles
formats.note: Separate ranked ladder with its own rating.

rules.gimmick: One Mega Evolution per battle. Champions has no Terastallization.

items.name: Mega Stone
items.effect: Lets the holder Mega Evolve once per battle. Champions requires the stone as a held item, so a Mega spends its item slot on it and cannot also carry a Life Orb or a Choice item.
items.note: Placeholder for the Megas whose stone Serebii has not named yet — the Legends Z-A forms, Mega Golisopod and Mega Baxcalibur. The 47 stones with published names are listed individually.

items.name: Leek
items.effect: Raises the critical-hit ratio of Farfetch'd or Sirfetch'd by 2 stages.
items.note: With Focus Energy or Dire Claw-style boosts, Sirfetch'd crits on demand — ignores enemy Defense boosts and Intimidate.

items.name: Rocky Helmet
items.effect: Attacker takes 1/6 of its max HP when it hits the holder with a contact move.
items.note: The single most important M-C item. Mega Golisopod and Mega Lucario Z are contact-locked; Rocky Helmet punishes both.

items.name: Air Balloon
items.effect: Holder is immune to Ground moves until it is hit by any damaging move, which pops the balloon.
items.note: Blanks Earthquake from Garchomp and Mega Garchomp Z, and lets a partner click spread Ground freely.

items.name: Red Card
items.effect: When the holder is hit by a damaging move, the attacker is switched out at random. Consumed.
items.note: Undoes a setup sweep and drags Megas out of position.

items.name: Eject Button
items.effect: When the holder is hit by a damaging move, it switches out immediately. Consumed.
items.note: Pivot out of an Intimidate cycle or a trapped matchup for free.

items.name: Binding Band
items.effect: Increases damage from binding moves (Whirlpool, Fire Spin, Infestation) to 1/6 per turn.
items.note: Niche, but a real win condition on trapping cores in singles.

items.name: Normal Gem
items.effect: Boosts the power of a Normal-type move by 30%. Consumed on use.
items.note: Sharp with Aerilate — Mega Salamence's Normal moves convert to Flying but still consume the Gem, stacking both boosts on Double-Edge.

items.name: Terrain Extender
items.effect: Terrain set by the holder lasts 8 turns instead of 5.
items.note: Turns a 5-turn terrain window into effectively the whole game.

items.name: Electric Seed
items.effect: Raises Defense by 1 stage on Electric Terrain. Consumed.
items.note: Pairs with Mega Raichu X's Electric Surge, the only Electric Terrain setter published so far.

items.name: Grassy Seed
items.effect: Raises Defense by 1 stage on Grassy Terrain. Consumed.
items.note: Pairs with Rillaboom's Grassy Surge.

items.name: Psychic Seed
items.effect: Raises Sp. Def by 1 stage on Psychic Terrain. Consumed.
items.note: Pairs with Indeedee's Psychic Surge.

items.name: Misty Seed
items.effect: Raises Sp. Def by 1 stage on Misty Terrain. Consumed.
items.note: No Misty Surge ability exists in the Champions roster, so this only comes online off the Misty Terrain move. The weakest of the four seeds.

items.name: Choice Scarf
items.effect: Raises Speed by 50% but locks the holder into the first move it uses.

items.name: Choice Band
items.effect: Raises Attack by 50% but locks the holder into the first move it uses.

items.name: Choice Specs
items.effect: Raises Sp. Atk by 50% but locks the holder into the first move it uses.

items.name: Life Orb
items.effect: Raises damage by 30%; holder loses 10% of max HP per damaging move.

items.name: Focus Sash
items.effect: Survives a KO from full HP with 1 HP. Consumed.

items.name: Assault Vest
items.effect: Raises Sp. Def by 50% but prevents the use of status moves.

items.name: Leftovers
items.effect: Restores 1/16 of max HP at the end of each turn.

items.name: Sitrus Berry
items.effect: Restores 25% of max HP when the holder drops below 50%. Consumed.

items.name: Safety Goggles
items.effect: Immune to powder moves and to weather chip damage.
items.note: Blocks powder moves and weather chip. Champions has no Spore, but Sleep Powder is here on the Venusaur and Victreebel lines, and Hypnosis is widespread — Goggles answers the powder half of that.

items.name: Covert Cloak
items.effect: Protects the holder from the secondary effects of moves.
items.note: Blanks Rock Slide flinches and Fake Out.

items.name: Clear Amulet
items.effect: Prevents the holder's stats from being lowered by other Pokémon.
items.note: The premier Intimidate answer for a physical Mega.

items.name: Mental Herb
items.effect: Cures Taunt, Encore, Torment, Attract and Disable. Consumed.

items.name: Weakness Policy
items.effect: Raises Attack and Sp. Atk by 2 stages when hit by a super-effective move. Consumed.

items.name: Expert Belt
items.effect: Raises the power of super-effective moves by 20%.

items.name: Wide Lens
items.effect: Raises accuracy by 10%.

items.name: Loaded Dice
items.effect: Multi-hit moves always hit 4-5 times.

items.name: Booster Energy
items.effect: Activates Protosynthesis or Quark Drive. Consumed.

items.name: Eviolite
items.effect: Raises Defense and Sp. Def by 50% for a Pokémon that can still evolve.

items.name: Light Clay
items.effect: Extends Reflect and Light Screen to 8 turns.

items.name: Throat Spray
items.effect: Raises Sp. Atk by 1 stage after using a sound move. Consumed.

items.name: Raichunite Y
items.effect: Lets the holder Mega Evolve once per battle. The stone occupies the item slot.
items.note: Mega Raichu Y. Confirmed from in-game screenshots — Serebii does not list the Champions-era stones.

items.name: Staraptite
items.effect: Lets the holder Mega Evolve once per battle. The stone occupies the item slot.
items.note: Mega Staraptor. Confirmed from in-game screenshots.

items.name: Dragoninite
items.effect: Lets the holder Mega Evolve once per battle. The stone occupies the item slot.
items.note: Mega Dragonite. Confirmed from in-game screenshots.

items.name: Baxcalibrite
items.effect: Lets Baxcalibur Mega Evolve.
items.note: Confirmed from ladder usage data; Serebii has not published the Champions-era stone names.

items.name: Golisopite
items.effect: Lets Golisopod Mega Evolve.
items.note: Confirmed from ladder usage data — 94.5% of Golisopod carry it.

items.name: Garchompite Z
items.effect: Lets Garchomp Mega Evolve into its Z form.
items.note: Confirmed from ladder usage data — 34.4% of Garchomp carry it.

items.name: Lucarionite Z
items.effect: Lets Lucario Mega Evolve into its Z form.
items.note: Confirmed from ladder usage data.

items.name: Floettite
items.effect: Lets Floette Mega Evolve.
items.note: Confirmed from ladder usage data.

items.name: Chople Berry
items.effect: Halves the damage of one super-effective Fighting-type move, then is consumed.
items.note: 42% of Kingambit carry this in M-C — Fighting is what answers it, and one Berry turns a knockout into a survivable hit.

items.name: Colbur Berry
items.effect: Halves the damage of one super-effective Dark-type move, then is consumed.
items.note: Seen on Indeedee and Farigiraf, whose Psychic typing makes Dark the obvious way to remove them.

usage.name: Garchomp
usage.why: Earthquake plus Rock Slide is the best spread-damage pairing in the format, and it now has a Mega Z form that flips it to a special sweeper.

usage.name: Basculegion
usage.why: Last Respects scales with your own fainted Pokémon and appeared on over 99% of tournament sets. The single highest-usage Pokémon of M-A.

usage.name: Kingambit
usage.why: Supreme Overlord plus priority Sucker Punch closes games. Defiant punishes Intimidate.

usage.name: Whimsicott
usage.why: Prankster Tailwind is the format's default speed control, with 68% co-usage alongside Garchomp.

usage.name: Sinistcha
usage.why: Hospitality plus Rage Powder soaks up a turn every game and heals its partner.

usage.name: Mega Metagross
usage.why: The best raw stat line of M-B: 145 Attack alongside 110 Speed and Tough Claws.

usage.name: Mega Mawile
usage.why: Huge Power doubles Attack to an effective 525. Gholdengo plus Mega Mawile is the format's safest core.

usage.name: Mega Charizard Y
usage.why: Drought plus Heat Wave, and its Flying typing means a Garchomp partner can click Earthquake freely — that pair was on 23.9% of all M-A teams.

usage.name: Gholdengo
usage.why: Good as Gold blanks every status move in the format, including Intimidate-adjacent support.

usage.name: Incineroar
usage.why: Intimidate plus Fake Out remains the safest support pick in doubles.

usage.name: Mega Swampert
usage.why: Swift Swim under rain outruns the entire unboosted format.

usage.name: Mega Staraptor
usage.why: Contrary turns Close Combat's drops into boosts, so it snowballs defensively while attacking.

usage.name: Sneasler
usage.why: Unburden plus Dire Claw's status chance makes it a nightmare once it is airborne.

usage.name: Annihilape
usage.why: Rage Fist grows every time it is hit, which doubles punishes spread moves.

usage.name: Farigiraf
usage.why: Armor Tail shuts off every priority move in the format, protecting a Trick Room turn.

usage.name: Mega Salamence
usage.why: 700 BST with 120 Speed and Aerilate Double-Edge. A two-time World Champion Mega returning into a format with no Steel-heavy top tier.

usage.name: Mega Garchomp Z
usage.why: 151 Speed and 141 Sp. Atk on a pure-Dragon body with Levitate. It outspeeds the entire format and ignores Ground moves, Spikes and terrain.

usage.name: Mega Lucario Z
usage.why: 164 Sp. Atk at 151 Speed, and Aura Guard halves incoming contact damage — offense and defense in one slot.

usage.name: Mega Golisopod
usage.why: Bug/Steel with 175 Defense and 150 Attack, Tough Claws, and 40 Speed that begs for Trick Room. First Impression at +30% is a genuine opening threat.

usage.name: Mega Baxcalibur
usage.why: 175 Attack and 115 HP, and Thermal Exchange makes it burn-proof and turns Fire coverage into a free Attack boost.

usage.name: Mega Absol Z
usage.why: Sharpness gives 50% on every slicing move, but frail defenses keep it out of the top tier.

usage.name: Rillaboom
usage.why: Grassy Surge plus priority Grassy Glide, and Grassy Terrain halves Earthquake — a direct structural answer to the Garchomp cores.

usage.name: Indeedee-F
usage.why: Psychic Surge blocks all priority — it turns off Sucker Punch, Fake Out, Grassy Glide and Aqua Jet at once, and Follow Me protects a Trick Room setter.

usage.name: Cinderace
usage.why: Libero gives it a free STAB on anything, and base 119 Speed sits above most of the format.

usage.name: Pincurchin
usage.why: Electric Surge on a base 15 Speed body — the natural Trick Room terrain setter. Mega Raichu X sets the same terrain far more aggressively; pick by which side of Trick Room you are on.

usage.name: Politoed
usage.why: The only Drizzle in the entire Champions roster, so every rain team in the format starts here. Perish Song gives it a second win condition when the rain plan stalls.

usage.name: Mega Raichu X
usage.why: Electric Surge plus 135 Attack and 110 Speed. The terrain blocks sleep and doubles Rising Voltage, and Fake Out into Encore is a genuine control turn. With Terrain Extender arriving in M-C this is the most immediately usable terrain setter in the game.

usage.name: Clefable
usage.why: One of only five Follow Me users in the format, and the only one with Magic Guard or Unaware. Redirection matters more in M-C because so many of the new Megas want one clean turn to set up.

usage.name: Conkeldurr
usage.why: 140 Attack at 45 Speed with Guts. The natural Trick Room partner for Mega Golisopod, and Wide Guard blanks the Rock Slide and Earthquake spam that punishes slow teams.

usage.name: Pelipper
usage.why: Drizzle plus Tailwind on one slot, and Wide Guard blanks the spread moves that define doubles. The faster of the two rain setters, where Politoed is the bulkier one.

notes.headline: M-C is a speed-tier reset and a terrain format waiting to happen.

threads.title: The 151 Speed ceiling
threads.body: Mega Garchomp Z and Mega Lucario Z both sit at base 151 Speed, well above the base 120 Mega Salamence and the old 110 Mega Metagross benchmark. Every Speed number you learned in M-B is now one tier too low. Either invest to outrun 151, or stop trying and go under them with Trick Room.

threads.title: Terrain arrived fully assembled
threads.body: M-C added Rillaboom (Grassy Surge) and Indeedee (Psychic Surge) in the same patch as Terrain Extender and all four Seeds. That is not a coincidence. Grassy Terrain halving Earthquake and Psychic Terrain blocking priority both attack the exact cores that defined M-B. Electric Terrain is already available on Mega Raichu X; Pincurchin adds a slow setter once it is published.

threads.title: Contact is a liability again
threads.body: Mega Golisopod, Mega Lucario Z, Mega Metagross and Mega Mawile all want to click contact moves. Rocky Helmet arrived in the same regulation. A single Rocky Helmet holder taxes four of the top Megas 1/6 per hit.

threads.title: Priority is contested
threads.body: Kingambit's Sucker Punch and Basculegion's Aqua Jet defined M-B endgames. Indeedee's Psychic Terrain turns both off outright, and Rillaboom's Grassy Glide jumps the queue. Whoever controls the terrain controls the last turn.

threads.title: Steel is suddenly crowded
threads.body: Mega Golisopod is Bug/Steel and Mega Lucario Z is Fighting/Steel, joining Mega Metagross, Mega Mawile, Gholdengo and Kingambit. Fire and Ground coverage is at a premium, and Mega Salamence's Aerilate Double-Edge is resisted by more of the field than its raw numbers suggest.

anti_meta.title: Rocky Helmet on a bulky redirector
anti_meta.body: Sinistcha or Amoonguss holding Rocky Helmet punishes Mega Golisopod's First Impression, Mega Metagross's Iron Head and Mega Mawile's Play Rough while still soaking a turn with Rage Powder.

anti_meta.title: Grassy Terrain over Garchomp cores
anti_meta.body: Rillaboom with Terrain Extender halves Earthquake for eight turns. Garchomp was the most-used Pokémon in both M-A and M-B; taxing its best move by 50% for the whole game is the highest-leverage structural choice in M-C.

anti_meta.title: Trick Room under the 151s
anti_meta.body: Mega Golisopod at 40 Speed with 175 Defense is a natural Trick Room abuser, and Farigiraf's Armor Tail protects the setup turn from every priority move. The two fastest Megas in the format become the two slowest.

anti_meta.title: Air Balloon on a Steel Mega
anti_meta.body: Mega Metagross or Mega Mawile with Air Balloon flips the Ground matchup that normally checks them, and lets your own Garchomp click Earthquake without clipping your partner.

anti_meta.title: Clear Amulet on your Mega
anti_meta.body: Intimidate from Incineroar is the cheapest way to blunt a physical Mega. Clear Amulet costs you a damage item but guarantees your Mega Salamence or Mega Baxcalibur hits at full Attack all game.

meta_teams.name: M-C Ladder Core
meta_teams.source: The six highest-usage Pokémon on the live Regulation M-C ladder, with the items, abilities and moves most sets actually run. Usage data from Pikalytics (CC BY-NC 4.0), 2026-09-10.
meta_teams.note: Rillaboom at 37.1% and Sneasler at 37.0% are the format, and every one of these six lists the others as its most common teammates. If you test a team against one thing, test it against this.

meta_teams.name: Big Six
meta_teams.source: The most-used structure of Regulation M-B; took five of the Top 8 at Japan Nationals. Also called Sunflower or Zard Slop.
meta_teams.note: Charizard Y + Garchomp was the single most common two-Pokemon core of the format, on roughly a quarter of sampled teams: Charizard is immune to Earthquake, so Garchomp can click it freely under Drought.

meta_teams.name: Indianapolis Sun
meta_teams.source: Arsal Puri's winning list from the 2026 Indianapolis Regional Championships (Regulation M-B).
meta_teams.note: A Big Six variant that cuts the priority core for Venusaur and Sinistcha. Slower and bulkier, and it beats the mirror by outlasting it.

meta_teams.name: Dual Mega Rain
meta_teams.source: Recurring M-B archetype. Politoed is the only Drizzle in the Champions roster, so every rain team in the format starts from it.
meta_teams.note: Swift Swim Mega Swampert outruns the entire unboosted format under rain. Mega Metagross is the backup plan for when the rain runs out.

meta_teams.name: Gholdengo + Mawile
meta_teams.source: Named in M-B analysis as the format's new safe core, filling the role Floette + Kingambit had in M-A.
meta_teams.note: Good as Gold turns off every status move aimed at the pair, and Huge Power gives Mawile an effective 525 Attack behind it.

meta_teams.name: Terrain Control
meta_teams.source: Built for M-C from the terrain pieces the regulation added. No ladder history yet.
meta_teams.note: Grassy Terrain halves Earthquake and Psychic Terrain switches off Sucker Punch, Fake Out and Aqua Jet. Both attack the cores that defined M-B, and Mega Golisopod is the Trick Room payoff underneath.

meta_teams.name: Z-Mega Hyper Offence
meta_teams.source: Built for M-C around the two base-151 Speed Megas the regulation added. No ladder history yet.
meta_teams.note: Both Z Megas sit above every established speed benchmark. The plan is to be faster than the answer and remove it before it moves.

predictions.title: Fire and Ice are the answer keys
predictions.call: Every serious team wants one Fire move and one Ice move, and the teams that skip them will keep losing to the same four Pokémon.
predictions.why: Against the weighted field, Ice averages 1.23x and Fire 1.20x — the two best attacking types in the format. Six of the thirty tracked threats are part Steel and four are part Dragon, and those two groups barely overlap in what answers them.
predictions.basis: Computed from the type chart against the usage table.

predictions.title: Normal is the worst attacking type, which is why Aerilate matters
predictions.call: Do not bring a Normal-type attacker. Do bring the one that stops being Normal.
predictions.why: Normal averages 0.64x into the field, last of the eighteen, with five Ghosts among the tracked threats walling it outright. Mega Salamence's Aerilate converts its Normal moves to Flying, which averages 1.13x — the conversion is worth more than the 20% power bonus attached to it.
predictions.basis: Computed. The Aerilate reading is judgement on top of it.

predictions.title: The middle speed tier is dead
predictions.call: Invest past 223 Speed or commit to Trick Room. Anything built to sit around 150 is choosing to move second.
predictions.why: The three Z Megas all reach 223 at full investment, then there is a 34-point gap to the next benchmark at 189. Nothing occupies the space between, so the usual approach of creeping a few points past a rival does not work here — you are either above the Z Megas or you are not.
predictions.basis: Computed from base Speed at 32 SP with a boosting alignment.

predictions.title: Flying/Steel is the best defensive shell in the format
predictions.call: Corviknight and Skarmory rise, and Mega Skarmory is underrated at the moment.
predictions.why: Flying/Steel takes 0.71x from the field's STAB moves, the lowest of any typing in the roster. It resists or is immune to the Fighting, Bug, Grass, Dragon, Psychic and Fairy attacks that the top threats lean on, and its Fire weakness is the one thing the format is genuinely loaded with — so it wants a partner that likes Fire aimed at it.
predictions.basis: Computed defensive average; the usage call is judgement.

predictions.title: Terrain will be under-adopted for the first month
predictions.call: Grassy and Psychic Terrain teams are stronger than their usage will show until people adjust.
predictions.why: M-C shipped Rillaboom, Indeedee and Pincurchin in the same patch as Terrain Extender and all four Seeds. Grassy Terrain halves Earthquake, and Garchomp was the most-used Pokemon of both prior regulations. Psychic Terrain switches off Sucker Punch, Fake Out, Aqua Jet and Grassy Glide, which is most of the format's priority. New mechanics take weeks to be taken seriously.
predictions.basis: Judgement, from what the regulation added together.

predictions.title: Contact moves are a liability this regulation
predictions.call: Rocky Helmet on a bulky redirector will over-perform.
predictions.why: Rocky Helmet arrived in the same regulation as Mega Golisopod and Mega Lucario Z, and joins Mega Metagross and Mega Mawile — four Megas whose main attacks all make contact. Aura Guard already halves contact damage in the other direction. One Helmet holder taxes a large share of the format 1/6 per hit.
predictions.basis: Judgement, from the item and Mega lists.

predictions.title: The projected placements are the weakest part of this page
predictions.call: Re-check everything here once the ladder has a month of M-C data.
predictions.why: Fourteen of the thirty tracked threats have no measured usage at all — they are placed by their stats and abilities, and given an assumed weight so they stay in the maths. The type and speed numbers above are arithmetic and will hold; the ranking of picks depends on those assumed weights and will move.
predictions.basis: A statement about the data, not a prediction about the game.
